rules.title: unbounded string copy
rules.why_flagged: unbounded string copy: the destination takes no length argument

rules.title: memcpy with untrusted size
rules.why_flagged: third argument is a variable, not sizeof(dest)
rules.flag_condition: flag when the size argument is not sizeof(<dest>)

rules.title: bounded copy misuse
rules.why_flagged: bounded copy whose size argument is derived from the source, not the destination
rules.flag_condition: flag when the size argument mentions the source, uses strlen(src), or uses sizeof(ptr) on a pointer rather than an array

rules.title: bounded formatted output
rules.why_flagged: bounded formatted output whose return value or NUL-termination is relied on
rules.flag_condition: flag when the return value is used as a length (it is the length that WOULD have been written), or when the call is in the _snprintf family, which gives no NUL guarantee. Scout table records this rule as CWE-787/120; CWE-787 is carried on the record

rules.title: untrusted read into fixed buffer
rules.why_flagged: read length argument is not sizeof(dest)
rules.flag_condition: flag when the length argument is not sizeof(<dest>)

rules.title: unbounded scanf
rules.why_flagged: scanf-family conversion into a fixed buffer
rules.flag_condition: flag when the format string contains %s or %[ WITHOUT a field width. This is a positive flag condition, not a skip clause: a format the extractor cannot read (built at runtime, in a macro, on another line) is EMITTED and the validator settles it

rules.title: inherently unsafe input
rules.why_flagged: call to a function with no safe usage, or to realpath, whose output buffer must hold PATH_MAX bytes
rules.flag_condition: gets/getwd are unconditional candidates; realpath is a candidate unless its second argument is NULL (the library allocates), and a caller buffer must be declared at least PATH_MAX - an earlier form matched only the NULL call, which is the safe one; the rest are candidates wherever they appear

rules.title: UAF/double-free
rules.why_flagged: release of a resource; the validator looks for a later use of it
rules.flag_condition: the candidate is the freeing call itself. Scout table records this rule as CWE-416/415; CWE-416 is carried on the record

rules.title: use-after-return
rules.why_flagged: a local address or a local buffer appears to escape the function
rules.flag_condition: also flag globals and out-params assigned &local. The third branch spans lines and is why this rule is multiline: ripgrep matches line by line unless -U/--multiline is passed, so this pattern silently returns nothing without it

rules.title: allocation size overflow
rules.why_flagged: allocation size is a computed expression
rules.flag_condition: flag when the size expression contains *, +, << or a non-size_t variable

rules.title: Rust unsafe
rules.why_flagged: raw-memory or FFI construct outside Rust's checked subset

rules.title: whole-function scan
rules.why_flagged: whole-function memory-safety pass, not a matched sink
rules.flag_condition: the seven questions of the whole-function pass: off-by-one heap/stack writes, Heartbleed-shaped over-reads, NULL-deref of unchecked returns, UAF that is not at a matched sink, division or modulo by zero, uninitialised use, and unchecked return values generally. A pass that found nothing closes on FP-WFS-CLEAN, with each of the seven answers cited in gates_evaluated Q1-Q7, and on no other code. A dismissal on the ground that a sibling candidate already covered the sink is refused (wfs_dismissal_by_sibling): that sentence is true of every MEM-WFS candidate the derivation can produce and so says nothing about this one
rules.derivation: Not grep-driven. After all six category files are written, take the distinct (file, function) pairs across the six emitted candidates/<category>.json files - deferred queues excluded, because a deferred candidate was never dispatched - whose function's language is in this rule's languages, and synthesize exactly one MEM-WFS candidate per pair. languages is c, cpp and rust: the seven questions are about raw memory, and over the eight garbage-collected languages it once listed too the pass cost one validator call per function with a hit and found nothing (all 21 on Python and Go in one end-to-end run closed FP-WFS-CLEAN), while Rust keeps it for its unsafe blocks and FFI. line is the function's opening line (function_range[0]); sink_text is read from that line off disk like any other candidate; why_flagged states the whole-function pass rather than a sink. MEM-WFS.emitted in coverage.json must equal that distinct-pair count (coverage invariant I5, which takes its pairs only from candidates in the languages coverage.json records for MEM-WFS), and the named function must match \b<name>\s*\( in the file beside it (wfs_function_absent). The scout table records this rule's CWE as `multi`; CWE-119 is the umbrella class carried on the record and the validator narrows it.
